title: 2017 真题 Text 3 · 间隔年能帮学生走得更远
description: 探讨间隔年对大学适应、专业选择和学费开销的积极作用。
author: 2017 English Exam
heroNote: 注意作者从学业表现与经济成本两个维度回应对间隔年的误解。

sentences.en: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year.
sentences.zhReference: 如今，社会普遍要求学生立刻上大学，再加上快节奏世界里日益提高的期望，常使学生完全忽略休学间隔年这一可能选择。

sentences.en: After all, if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year, doesn’t it?
sentences.zhReference: 毕竟，如果认识的每个人秋天都去上大学，自己晚一年似乎很傻，不是吗？

sentences.en: And after going to school for 12 years, it doesn’t feel natural to spend a year doing something that isn’t academic.
sentences.zhReference: 而且，上了十二年学之后，花一年做与学业无关的事也会让人觉得不自然。

sentences.en: But while this may be true, it’s not a good enough reason to condemn gap years.
sentences.zhReference: 但即便如此，也不足以成为否定间隔年的理由。

sentences.en: There’s always a constant fear of falling behind everyone else on the socially perpetuated “race to the finish line,” whether that be toward graduate school, medical school or a lucrative career.
sentences.zhReference: 人们总害怕在社会不断强化的“冲向终点”竞赛中落后于他人，无论终点是研究生院、医学院还是高收入事业。

sentences.en: But despite common misconceptions, a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits—in fact, it probably enhances it.
sentences.zhReference: 但与常见误解相反，间隔年不会妨碍学业成功，事实上还可能助益学业。

sentences.en: Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not.
sentences.zhReference: 美国和澳大利亚的研究表明，休过间隔年的学生通常比没休过的学生更充分地做好大学准备，在大学的表现也更好。

sentences.en: Rather than pulling students back, a gap year pushes them ahead by preparing them for independence, new responsibilities and environmental changes—all things that first-year students often struggle with the most.
sentences.zhReference: 间隔年并非拖后腿，而是让学生为独立生活、新责任和环境变化做好准备，帮助他们走在前面；这些都是大一新生最常遇到的难题。

sentences.en: Gap year experiences can lessen the blow when it comes to adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment, making it easier to focus on academics and activities rather than acclimation blunders.
sentences.zhReference: 当学生适应大学、进入全新环境时，间隔年的经历可以减轻冲击，使他们更容易专注于学业和活动，而不是在适应过程中屡屡犯错。

sentences.en: If you’re not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then consider its financial impact on future academic choices.
sentences.zhReference: 如果你仍不相信休学一年探索兴趣的内在价值，那就考虑一下它对未来学业选择的经济影响。

sentences.en: According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 80 percent of college students end up changing their majors at least once.
sentences.zhReference: 根据美国国家教育统计中心的数据，近百分之八十的大学生最终至少会转一次专业。

sentences.en: This isn’t surprising, considering the basic mandatory high school curriculum leaves students with a poor understanding of the vast academic possibilities that await them in college.
sentences.zhReference: 这并不奇怪，因为高中基础必修课程使学生对大学里等待他们的广泛学科选择所知甚少。

sentences.en: Many students find themselves listing one major on their college applications, but switching to another after taking college classes.
sentences.zhReference: 许多学生申请大学时填报一个专业，上过大学课程后却转到了另一个专业。

sentences.en: It’s not necessarily a bad thing, but depending on the school, it can be costly to make up credits after switching too late in the game.
sentences.zhReference: 这不一定是坏事，但要看学校而定：若转专业太晚，补修学分可能代价高昂。

sentences.en: At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department.
sentences.zhReference: 例如，在波士顿学院，如果从其他院系转入护理学院，就得多读一年。

vocabulary.meaning: 如果你转入；倒装虚拟条件句

sentences.en: Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on.
sentences.zhReference: 先休一年间隔年把方向想清楚，有助于日后减轻压力、节省费用。
